content.overview: Public Interest Litigation relaxes traditional locus standi so that a person acting bona fide may move the court for enforcement of constitutional or legal rights of persons who cannot approach the court themselves; it is a rule of standing, not a new substantive writ.
content.study: PIL is a rule of standing, not a new writ. The petitioner need not be personally aggrieved if they act in genuine public interest for the benefit of the disadvantaged or for enforcement of public duties (S.P. Gupta; Bandhua Mukti Morcha — orientation names only; verify reports). Private disputes, contractual rivalries, and personal grudges dressed as PIL fail the bona fide public-interest test and belong under limits-and-costs. Link standing to the chosen forum under Articles 32 and 226.
